rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. A midrange temperature leaves room to explore temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

Raise temperature while keeping the gradient fixed to test temperature-dependent selectivity of the single critical pair. The current 8.30-minute elution window leaves ample time margin, so improving that pair could reach the maximum CRF without slowing the gradient.

The peak-width and retention patterns suggest the critical pair reversed order between 40 and 50 C; moving to 55 C may open that separation further. A modestly shallower gradient should help preserve resolution elsewhere while keeping the last peak near or below 10 minutes.
Slightly flatten the gradient at the best temperature to try to lift the remaining R = 1.47 pair above 1.5. The last peak at 8.60 minutes leaves room for this change without an expected time penalty.

The shallower gradient reduced critical-pair resolution, so test a steeper gradient at 55 C instead. This should improve that pair and shorten elution, while the neighboring R = 2.18 pair appears to have enough margin for the change.

Injection 5 reached the maximum CRF; retain it as the benchmark and test a shorter gradient for faster fully resolved elution. Watch the two marginal pairs closely, especially the pair currently at R = 1.59.

The 10-minute gradient lost resolution, so restore tG to 12 minutes and test a higher starting organic fraction instead. This may shorten retention while the slightly shallower slope helps protect the newly limiting pair; injection 5 remains the maximum-score benchmark.

Keep injection 5 as the maximum-score benchmark and explore a substantially faster, hotter gradient. This tests whether the currently limiting pair can reverse elution order and regain separation, opening a faster fully resolved operating region.

Explore the cooler selectivity region, where the pair that crossed between 40 and 50 C may become fully separated again. Keep the scouting gradient fixed to isolate temperature effects and look for an alternative region with enough resolution margin to shorten later.

Return to the successful 55 C region and test a narrower gradient window. The higher starting organic fraction should reduce retention, while the shallower slope may recover the resolution lost when only phi0 was raised.

Test a shorter gradient at an intermediate cooler temperature to explore a different selectivity region rather than continue compressing the marginal 55 C separation. Injection 5 remains the maximum-CRF benchmark.

Refine injection 7 by lowering the endpoint one step, making the gradient slightly shallower to recover its R = 1.29 pair. This may achieve full resolution with a last-peak time slightly shorter than the maximum-score benchmark.

Lower the endpoint one more step to lift injection 12's R = 1.47 pair above threshold while its other critical pair has some margin at R = 1.60. This targets another maximum-score method with potentially better minimum resolution than injection 5, still comfortably below 10 minutes.

With two maximum-score methods secured, explore a faster high-temperature region using a higher starting organic fraction. This tests whether the reversed central pair seen in injection 8 can separate while a gentler slope restores its neighboring pair.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step to try to widen the reversed central pair, the only unresolved pair in injection 14. Monitor the early pair at R = 2.62, since higher initial organic may compress it as retention shortens.

The faster 60 C region is constrained by multiple pairs, so test the unexplored low-temperature boundary for a different elution-order pattern. A broad 10-minute gradient should keep all compounds observable and may reveal another route to faster full resolution; injection 5 remains the benchmark.

Test a shallower gradient at 60 C to recover the central separation while retaining the stronger temperature-driven separation of the other critical pair. This targets another fully resolved method with the last peak estimated just below 10 minutes; injection 5 remains the faster maximum-score benchmark.

Shorten the programmed gradient while preserving injection 5's successful slope of 0.075 organic fraction per minute. The gradient endpoint reaches the outlet at 8.65 minutes, after the benchmark's last peak at 7.60 minutes, so this should retain full resolution without requiring 95% organic.

Test an intermediate starting organic fraction in the fast 60 C region to assess whether the reversed central pair can reach full resolution without compressing its neighbor excessively. The maximum-score methods remain secured; this injection specifically seeks a shorter fully resolved elution window.

Preserve the successful gradient slope through the crowded peak region, then hold at 50% organic to test a shorter programmed gradient and lower endpoint. Only the well-isolated last peak should be affected appreciably; monitor whether it still elutes within 10 minutes.

Refine the fully resolved injection 13 with a slightly steeper slope, intermediate between injections 12 and 13. This should shorten its elution window while keeping both critical pairs above 1.5; injection 5 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Seek more resolution margin around the maximum score by flattening injection 10's gradient enough to improve its limiting central pair. The other critical pair was at R = 1.76, and the last peak should remain below 10 minutes; injection 5 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Lower the endpoint one step to bring injection 22's R = 1.41 pair above 1.5, while its other critical pair retains margin at R = 1.74. This targets a maximum-score alternative with improved resolution margin and an expected last peak below 10 minutes.

Refine injection 23 with a slightly shallower slope to balance its two critical resolutions and improve the minimum-resolution margin. The last peak is expected around 9.3 minutes, preserving maximum CRF; injection 5 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Finish with an untested grid method that preserves the fastest confirmed fully resolved gradient slope and keeps the endpoint beyond the elution window. It should reproduce the 7.60-minute last peak and maximum CRF of injection 5 with a shorter programmed gradient and lower final organic fraction.
